vote.summary: Propose parallel chunked pgvector v2 with deterministic FTS+vector RRF, shared query-embedding cache, and per-job authorized context snapshot. External vector DB, result cache, in-place v1 alteration, and separate reranker are deferred or rejected. No blocker for the plan; benchmark inputs remain unknown until the code phase.

Deterministic lexical and vector fusion without comparing raw score scales, with separate KB capacity and diversity
Deterministic heading/paragraph chunking, size/overlap/IDs, parent provenance, replacement/delete, citations, and flood control
Durable/recoverable batched embedding with shared admission, bounded retry, response/dimension validation, and per-item stale-write guard
Cold-query latency reduction via safe query-embedding cache and FTS overlap, with no SQLAlchemy session shared across threads
One immutable authorized context snapshot per job reused by both agents, with identity and expiry

vote.proposed_artifact:
Decision artifact: parallel chunked pgvector v2 with deterministic hybrid FTS+vector; plan only, no code.

Target architecture
- Keep the v1 whole-document store for rollback and keyword-only fallback; add a parallel chunked v2 pgvector store.
- Both logical agents on the same approved model consume one per-job authorized context snapshot created from one retrieval call.
- Read path: live auth/source predicates before limits, then FTS pool (40 ticket/comment candidates plus 12-20 KB candidates) and vector pool (40 ticket/comment candidates plus 12-20 KB candidates), then deterministic RRF(k=60), deterministic tie-break by (source_type, source_id, chunk_id), max two chunks per parent/ticket, final 6-10 passages, then snapshot.
- No result cache, no external vector DB, no second model, no cross-model fallback, and no learned reranker.

Schema and indexes
- New table ticket_search_documents_v2: id identity PK; source_type; source_id; chunk_id; chunk_index; content; content_hash; embedding vector(configured dimension); token_estimate; created_at; updated_at; UNIQUE(source_type, source_id, chunk_id); CHECK(chunk_index >= 0).
- Indexes: HNSW on embedding using vector_cosine_ops; GIN on to_tsvector using the same FTS configuration as v1; btree on (source_type, source_id) for replace/delete/reconciliation.
- Dimension lock/preflight: migration bakes the configured dimension; startup and migration fail on mismatch; model or dimension change requires a new table/version, never ALTER of the vector column.
- Cleanup is additive only; v1 is retained through the rollback window and retired only after the divergence and data-retention gate passes.

Chunking
- Deterministic heading/paragraph split; target 350-500 tokens, max 600, about 50 token overlap at paragraph boundaries; short descriptions and comments remain single chunks.
- chunk_id = sha256(source_type|source_id|chunk_index); content_hash covers source content and provenance-relevant state.
- Atomic source replacement: delete old chunks for the source and insert new chunks in one transaction only after all batch embeddings succeed and pre-commit revalidation confirms source state, hash, and embedding identity are current.
- Edits, deletion, unpublish, or private-policy changes trigger the same replacement path.
- Flood control: retrieval caps at two chunks per parent/ticket; storage has a configurable max chunks per source family with alert/stop, never silent truncation.

Embedding batches and recovery
- Use durable ai_jobs embedding refresh with lease fields, lease expiry, attempts, status, and a reaper to recover expired leases after worker death or DB restart; periodic sweep covers missed wake-ups.
- Batch size 32, or the provider-contract maximum if lower; batches go through the existing shared provider admission, RPM/TPM/daily budget controls.
- Max two attempts with jitter; malformed, wrong-dimension, or toxic items are isolated and retried separately.
- Validate response shape, embedding dimension, and identity; per-item current-hash and source-state check immediately before commit; stale items are skipped or re-enqueued.
- Never hold a DB transaction or request session across a provider call; each operation uses separate sessions/connections.

Hybrid algorithm
- Apply portal, private, assignee, KB, and authority predicates before any candidate limit.
- Generate rank positions within each authorized pool; fusion uses RRF = 1/(60+rank), so raw score scales are never compared.
- Ties broken deterministically by (source_type, source_id, chunk_id); KB capacity and diversity are kept separate; final passage cap is 6-10.
- Cold query: run FTS immediately with its own session while computing the query embedding; run vector search in another session after embedding returns.

Caches
- Implement shared PostgreSQL query-vector cache: tenant + normalized query hash + embedding identity + dimension; value is the embedding only, no raw query; TTL 30-60 minutes; purge expired rows.
- Cache hits only reuse the query embedding; every retrieval still reruns live authorization and source validation.
- Persistent vectors and caches inherit source classification; no raw query/ticket/prompt/secret/provider body in routine telemetry.
- G1 local cache assessed but not required; G3 result cache deferred/rejected because auth and corpus invalidation are unsafe.

Per-job snapshot
- Add job_context_snapshots: snapshot_id, job_id, corpus_identity_hash, source/auth version, embedding identity, exact authorized items and citations, created_at, expires_at.
- Build once per job from the retrieval result; both agents read the same immutable snapshot.
- Re-retrieve only when corpus, source, auth, or embedding identity changes; expired snapshots are never used; generated output is never added as evidence.

File-level changes planned
- Migrations: v2 tables/indexes, dimension lock check, query-vector cache and snapshot tables; no destructive operations.
- ticket_vectors.py: chunking, v2 writes, RRF retrieval, cache and snapshot helpers.
- API and jobs: embedding refresh jobs, lease/reaper, query handler, snapshot creation and expiry.
- Settings/Helm/docs: flags, batch size, TTLs, gates, rollback, and operational docs.
- Tests: unit, integration, adversarial, benchmark, and failure injection suites.

Migration and rollback
- Phase 1: preflight and benchmark.
- Phase 2: additive v2 schema, dual-write, bounded backfill.
- Phase 3: hybrid reads behind feature flag with shadow comparison.
- Phase 4: cutover to v2 while retaining v1 dual-write.
- Phase 5: retire v1 only after no divergence, zero stale/unauthorized evidence, and configured retention.
- Rollback is a flag flip to the v1/keyword path; dual-write continues until retirement.

Tests, SLOs, and metrics
- Gates: warm retrieval p95 < 250 ms; cached-query retrieval p95 < 400 ms; cold embedding+retrieval p95 < 2 s; index freshness p95 < 60 s; zero stale/unauthorized evidence; relevance not below baseline.
- Metrics: Recall@5/10, MRR or NDCG@10, relevant published-KB presence, duplicate-parent rate, citation/action grounding, no-answer precision, latency p50/p95/p99, query-cache hit/age, batch utilization, provider latency, index lag/retry/stale count, v1-v2 divergence, rows/query, DB CPU/IO/locks/index size, prompt tokens, core API latency under search/backfill.
- Adversarial suite: portal/private/cross-assignee/unapproved poison, stale after edit/delete/unpublish, provider timeout/partial/malformed/wrong-dimension, toxic item, worker death, missed wake-up, DB restart, stale query cache/snapshot, chunk flooding, duplicates, and no-answer queries.

Option ledger
- A: tune current store - early phase only.
- B: hybrid FTS+vector - implement now.
- C: parallel chunked v2 - preferred target.
- D: in-place v1 alteration - reject; risky index/uniqueness migration and poor rollback.
- E: external vector DB - defer; trigger at 100k-1M chunk benchmark failure or measured gate failure.
- F1: deterministic RRF - default.
- F2: same-LLM rerank - defer; only if NDCG/grounding gate fails and latency/cost/injection risk is accepted.
- F3: separate reranker - reject; violates one-model constraint.
- G1: local query-vector cache - assessed, optional only.
- G2: PostgreSQL query-vector cache - implement.
- G3: result cache - defer/reject.
- G4: per-job snapshot - required.
- Target hybrid: B+C+G2+G4+F1; early phase A+B; optional F2 later with evidence.

Unknowns and stop conditions
- Unknown: corpus size, QPS, repeated-query rate, document lengths, batch contract, provider latency, DB headroom, labelled retrieval relevance. All bootstrap numbers are test inputs.
- Stop: relevance below baseline; any latency or freshness gate missed; any stale/unauthorized evidence; v1-v2 divergence beyond threshold; dimension/provider mismatch; failure injection not recovered; rollback not verified. No cutover or retirement until gates pass.
